newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks consolidate at opening, above 2,300.
newsitem.headline: French stocks consolidate at opening, above 2,300.

text.p: French shares staged an orderly retreat at the opening on Monday, with modest profit taking after last week's substantial gains. "Friday's volume was colossal," said one broker.
The market would likely consolidate around the psychologically-important 2,300 level before attacking the previous historic high at 2,360.98, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 7.61 points or 0.33 percent at 2,308.05 at 0925 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,311 from 2,319 on Friday's close.

"The market's got a good feel to it," said one broker. Paris is still considered cheap compared to other markets and should attract new money as U.S. funds, flush with cash, look for opportunities abroad in the New Year

Sports goods company Salomon slumps 6.41 percent on first half results, considered disappointing. One broker has pencilled in full-year 1996 earnings growth of 12 percent, while the company posted a first-half increase of 9.6 percent.
Insurer UAP, down 0.72 percent at 138.10 francs, continues to lead volume stocks.
Eurotunnel continues fall, down four percent, as the market waits for safety approval for passenger traffic to resume.
Renault limps, down two percent. The market expects the carmaker to show poor November car sales figures, due today. The stock has consistently underperformed relative to PSA Peugeot Citroen.
Food group Saint-Louis gains 1.5 percent to 1,345 francs after announcing sale of stake in Panzalim prepared foods firm to Danone for about 2.9 billion francs.

Missiles-to-books conglomerate Lagardere eases 1.33 percent to 155.9 francs. French newspapers report the European Commission plans to set stiff conditions on approving its bid for electronics firm Thomson SA and a state recapitalisation that is part of the deal.
